title: The Share of a Lapsed Micro Market Balance Handed Back to the Client
content:
A client of the Unattended Micro Market Program that has funded its micro market repeatedly is handed back more of a lapsed balance, and its settlement record over the trailing year settles how much.

## Points of judgement

**When is the whole balance handed back?** Where the client has funded at or above 2 subsidy lots on the agreement and settled at or above 3 market settlement invoices over the twelve months to the day the credit is worked out, the full credit share of 100 per cent is handed back.

**When is part of it retained?** Where the client has funded at or above 2 subsidy lots on the agreement and settled below 3 market settlement invoices over those twelve months, the retained credit share of 85 per cent is handed back.

**And where the client has funded fewer lots?** Where the agreement carries below 2 subsidy lots, no such change to the share is made.

## The boundaries in figures

The repeat funding count is 2 subsidy funding lots on the agreement, counted over the whole life of the agreement: exactly 2 meets it, 1 does not. The prompt settlement count is 3 settlement payments over the twelve months to the day the credit is worked out: exactly 3 meets it, 2 does not.

*Hypothetical.* An agreement carrying 4 funding lots whose client settled 5 invoices over the trailing year hands back the whole of an unspent balance of 3000.00 USD. The same agreement, had its client settled only 2 invoices over that year, would hand back 2550.00 USD. An agreement carrying a single funding lot reaches neither condition.
